body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.25**: the Y2 plays videos. This is an early version of video playback: expect bugs, and please report them.

## What's new
- **Videos (early version)**. Copy video files onto Internal Storage or the SD card, the same way as songs; any folder works, and a folder of your own such as `Videos` keeps them together. After the next scan **Videos** appears on Home, with a picture of each film. A film plays on Now Playing: Play/Pause, Previous/Next, the wheel and the volume work as for a song, a button press shows the title and a time line, and a film goes on where you left it. The screen stays on while a film plays. Films never show up among your songs, albums or shuffles.
- **Subtitles** show when the file carries a text track, or when a subtitle file with the same name lies beside the film (`Film.mkv` and `Film.srt`, `.ass`, `.ssa` or `.vtt`).
- **The best format: MP4 with H.264 video and AAC sound, 640×360, up to 30 pictures a second.** The screen has 480×360 pixels, so a bigger picture looks no better, only fills the storage and uses more battery. About 1 Mbit/s is plenty: a two-hour film is then under 1 GB.
- **What plays**: `.mp4` `.m4v` `.mov` `.mkv` `.webm` `.avi`. H.264 and MPEG-4 (Xvid, DivX) are decoded by the player's video chip, up to 1920×1080. VP8, VP9, DivX 3 and H.263 are decoded by the processor and are only smooth at small sizes (about 640×360).
- **What does not play**: H.265/HEVC, AV1, DTS sound, picture subtitles (DVD, Blu-ray), files with a picture and no sound. Convert such films first, and big ones too: see [Videos on the Y2](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/VIDEO.md) for a ready command and HandBrake settings.
- **A song tagged "Pop/Rock" is now in Pop and in Rock** ([Y2Reborn #124](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Reborn/issues/124)). Tagging programs that join several genres with "/" are understood; "Singer/Songwriter" stays one genre.

## How fast it is (measured on one player)
- H.264 1280×720 at 30 pictures a second and 1920×1080 at 24: no picture dropped, the player used about 60 % of one of its four processor cores.
- Xvid 1280×720 at 25 pictures a second: no picture dropped, 57 % of one core.
- VP9 640×360: no picture dropped, 80 % of one core. Bigger VP9 files will stutter.

## Known issues
- **Video is new.** Sleep and wake while a film is open have not been tested, and nobody has measured how long the battery lasts with films. Leave Now Playing before you put the player to sleep if you see trouble.
- Over Bluetooth the sound comes a little later than the picture (the headphones' own delay).
- The first text subtitle and the default sound track are used; there is no menu to choose another or to turn subtitles off.
- Skins show their own lists, but the film itself always uses Reborn's own screen.
- Interlaced Xvid/DivX films and 10-bit H.264 are decoded by the processor and may stutter above DVD size.
- On a card formatted as FAT32 a file can't be larger than 4 GB.
- Everything listed for [Beta 9.3.24](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/releases/tag/baseline-235) still applies.
- Something wrong? Send an error report (Settings → System → Error Reports). **Restore Previous System** (Settings → System → About, tap Version seven times, then Diagnostics) takes you back to the version you had, with your data kept.

More details in plain words: **[Beta 9.3.25 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-9.3.25.md)**.

<!-- github-only -->

## Converting a film for the Y2
With [FFmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org) (free, every computer):

```
ffmpeg -i film.mkv -vf "scale=-2:360" -r 30 -c:v libx264 -profile:v high -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 23 -c:a aac -b:a 160k film.mp4
```

For an old 4:3 film use `scale=480:360`. With [HandBrake](https://handbrake.fr): preset **Fast 480p30**, format MP4, video encoder H.264, and set the height to 360 under Dimensions. Keep the subtitle as a separate `.srt` file with the film's name, or add it as a text track; burnt-in picture subtitles from DVDs and Blu-rays do not show otherwise.

A film converted like this needs roughly 8 MB a minute. Films up to 1920×1080 play as they are when they use H.264 (8 bit) or Xvid/DivX; they only cost more battery and storage.

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → System → Software Update → **Update Now**. Your music, playlists, settings, Wi-Fi networks and Bluetooth pairings stay. (On Beta 9.2.8 and older: Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.)

## Install with the Innioasis Updater (easiest)
The community **Innioasis Updater CE** installs Y2Linux for you, on **Windows, macOS and Linux**. No SP Flash Tool needed.

1. Download Innioasis Updater CE for your computer from [innioasis.app](https://innioasis.app/guide.html#download-updater) and open it.
2. Choose **Y2**, then **Reborn (Y2Linux)** and the latest release.
3. Click **Install / Restore**, switch the Y2 off and connect it when the updater asks. Wait until it confirms, then unplug.
4. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** `system.img` from the Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0 into the **Firmware** folder on **Internal Storage**. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

Step-by-step guides for each computer: [Reborn (Y2Linux) install guide](https://innioasis.app/guides/reborn-y2linux-y2.html). The way back to stock is in the updater too: choose **Y2** and **Original Software**.

## Install with SP Flash Tool
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.9.3.25-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (only this version works; it is also your way back to stock).

1. Unpack both.
2. SP Flash Tool → **Download Only** → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.
3. Click Download and connect the switched-off Y2; wait for the green tick.
4. Unplug and press Power: the player sets up its Internal Storage (a few seconds), then Y2Linux and Reborn start, music works.
5. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** (don't move) `system.img` from the Innioasis package into the **Firmware** folder on **Internal Storage**. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

## How it was tested
The platform's full check and Reborn's tests passed, and so did the tests of the release images. On one player: this build was installed over the air; H.264 pictures from the video chip were compared with a software decoder and are identical (130 of 135 standard test streams and nine films); Xvid/DivX pictures differ from it by at most 5 of 255 brightness steps, which the format allows (ten films). Films were played in Reborn and checked by screen captures. Not tested: sleep and wake with a film open, battery life with films, damaged files, players with the other screen type.

## Files
- `Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.9.3.25-first-install.zip`: images, scatter files and checksums for SP Flash Tool. The data image has no SSH key (developers: `tools/production/first_owner.py`).
- `manifest.json`, `manifest.sig`, `rootfs.ext4.gz`, `bootimg.img.gz`, `recovery.img.gz`: the signed over-the-air update (Ed25519 key `platform-v1-release-20261015`, sequence 16200).
- `Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.9.3.25-sources-buildroot-legal-info.tar` (licences, manifests, this project's packages) and the third-party, toolchain and Linux sources linked below: corresponding sources. Our own code: Y2Linux and Y2Reborn at tag `baseline-248`. The video chip is driven by this project's own driver; no MediaTek video code is on the player. The speaker amplifier driver is Chris Hendrickson's GPL-2.0 AW87559 driver. The headphone profiles are AutoEq results (MIT, Jaakko Pasanen); their licence ships with them.
- `SHA256SUMS` for the attached files.

Beta software: use at your own risk. Not affiliated with Innioasis, MediaTek, Awinic, Last.fm, AutoEq, Strawberry, MusicBee, HandBrake, FFmpeg or Google. Noto Sans CJK is licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.25

body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.24**: Bluetooth always sends standard SBC, and the battery shows the right level after charging while switched off.

## Fixed
- **Battery level after charging while switched off** ([#113](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/113)). A player that was charged while off and started later, off the charger, still showed the old lower percentage, which looked like a drained battery. It now shows the level it measures at the start.

## Changed
- **SBC XQ is gone; Bluetooth sends standard SBC** ([Y2Reborn #123](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Reborn/issues/123)). XQ and XQ+ sent much more data than headphones and speakers on a busy or weak link could take, and the music stuttered. The **SBC Quality** row in the service menu is removed. A player that was set to XQ uses standard SBC after the update, with nothing to do. **SBC Auto Rate** stays. AAC and LDAC are unchanged.

## Behind the scenes
- **Error reports now show Bluetooth's data rate over time**, so a stutter can be matched to what the link did ([#99](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/issues/99), [Y2Reborn #87](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Reborn/issues/87)).

Everything from [Beta 9.3.23](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/releases/tag/baseline-234) is included: Now Playing's progress wave in the cover's colour, the screen that stays dark after a sleep that didn't work, steadier Bluetooth on a weak signal and Wi-Fi on channels 12 and 13.

## Known issues
- A network on channel 12 or 13 may need a second scan to appear.
- Music can stutter for a few seconds while Wi-Fi switches on.
- Far from the headphones the music still pauses when the signal is lost; it no longer rushes afterwards.
- A charge-only USB cable only charges. If your computer doesn't see the player, try a cable that transfers data with a phone.
- Skins with their own fonts (Luna XP, Winamp and others) show boxes instead of Chinese, Japanese and Korean titles.
- After a sleep, Bluetooth headphones reconnect within a few seconds of waking. Headphones that went back to a phone meanwhile must be picked again in Settings → Bluetooth.
- WPA3-only Wi-Fi networks can't be joined; a "WPA2/WPA3 mixed" setting on the router works.
- One audiobook file longer than about 36 hours may not play or not show up; split it into parts of up to 30 hours.
- Some players turned off by themselves during playback; the cause isn't found yet.
- Something wrong? Send an error report (Settings → System → Error Reports). **Restore Previous System** (Settings → System → About, tap Version seven times, then Diagnostics) takes you back to the version you had, with your data kept.

More details in plain words: **[Beta 9.3.24 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-9.3.24.md)**.

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.23

body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.22**: the screen no longer comes on by itself after a sleep that didn't work.

## Fixed
- **The screen turned on by itself every few minutes** on some players. The player goes to sleep by itself when it is paused; when that didn't work, it switched the screen on again, and tried again a little later. The screen now stays dark, and the next try waits longer. Pressing Power still lights it at once.

Everything from [Beta 9.3.21](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/releases/tag/baseline-232) is included: steadier Bluetooth on a weak signal, Wi-Fi on channels 12 and 13, the battery fix for players without Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, and the SD card fix.

- After a sleep, Bluetooth headphones reconnect within a few seconds of waking. Headphones that went back to a phone meanwhile must be picked again in Settings → Bluetooth.
- WPA3-only Wi-Fi networks can't be joined; a "WPA2/WPA3 mixed" setting on the router works.

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.22

body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.21**: steadier Bluetooth on a weak signal, Wi-Fi on channels 12 and 13, battery and SD card fixes.

## What's new
- **Bluetooth keeps off your Wi-Fi's channel.** Both share one antenna; while Wi-Fi is connected, Bluetooth now leaves the Wi-Fi network's channels alone.
- **FLAC and Opus songs have a bitrate** (skins can show it). For songs already in your library, run Settings → System → Reset & Maintenance → **Rebuild Music Library** once.

## Fixed
- **Bluetooth dropped out and then played fast** when the signal got weak (far from the headphones, a body in between). After a pause in the link the player sent everything it had missed in one burst. The music now simply continues where it stopped.
- **Bluetooth headphones could go silent** after the player was busy for a moment. The player now always sends something while music is on, silence if need be.
- **Starting music on slow Bluetooth headphones** could fail with an error although the headphones were about to answer. The player now waits longer for them.
- **Wi-Fi networks on channel 12 or 13 never showed up.** The player now listens on these channels too; no setting needed.
- **The battery was empty in the morning** on players whose Wi-Fi and Bluetooth never started: such a player could not go to sleep. It sleeps now.
- **An exFAT SD card could freeze until a restart** when a damaged or half-copied file on it was read.

## Known issues
- A network on channel 12 or 13 may need a second scan to appear.
- Far from the headphones the music still pauses when the signal is lost; it no longer rushes afterwards.
- A charge-only USB cable only charges. If your computer doesn't see the player, try a cable that transfers data with a phone.
- Skins with their own fonts (Luna XP, Winamp and others) show boxes instead of Chinese, Japanese and Korean titles.
- After a sleep, Bluetooth headphones reconnect within a few seconds of waking. Headphones that went back to a phone meanwhile must be picked again in Settings → Bluetooth.
- WPA3-only Wi-Fi networks can't be joined; a "WPA2/WPA3 mixed" setting on the router works.
- One audiobook file longer than about 36 hours may not play or not show up; split it into parts of up to 30 hours.

## What's new
- **Previous Chapter / Next Chapter** for audiobooks: hold Select on Now Playing. They jump to the chapter start however far away it is.
- **SBC Auto Rate** in Diagnostics (Settings → System → About, tap Version seven times): lets SBC headphones lower the rate when the signal gets weak instead of stuttering. Off by default; if you hear Bluetooth dropouts, please try it and tell us.

- **An album started from the album page played shuffled** when Shuffle was on. A single album now always plays in order; playlists and mixed songs still shuffle.
- **Skins: Cover Flow titles stood still** while the covers slid. They now glide and fade with the covers.
- **Wi-Fi after waking** could give up on a network that was right there and restart, and after a sleep without headphones the player kept looking for them for almost a minute, which held Wi-Fi up. It now looks once and keeps trying a network it can see.
- **A very long audiobook file was missing without a word**: one file of more than about 50 hours is too big for the player to read. Settings → Library now counts it as a file that couldn't be read.

name: Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.19

body:
**Y2Linux 1.0 Beta 9.3.18**: USB that always reconnects, a new skin and quicker settings.

## What's new
- **Luna XP skin**: blue title bars, a green start button and rolling hills, made by eNKay. Pick it in Settings → Skin.
- **Quick settings from the Quick Menu**: hold Power to open the Quick Menu, then hold Select on Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or Brightness to jump straight to that setting.
- **Sort an artist's albums your way**: Settings → Customize → Browsing → Artist's Albums: Oldest First, Newest First or A to Z.
- **Cover Flow matches your skin**: its colours, fonts and cover shape now follow the skin you picked.
- **Updates without Wi-Fi**: when Wi-Fi is off, Software Update shows **Connect to Wi-Fi** and takes you there, instead of a check that can't work.
- **Songs the player can't play**: if your card has files the player can't play (WMA or DSD, for example), Settings → Library now tells you how many and which kind, so they no longer just seem to be missing.
- **For skin makers**: `{bitrate}` shows a song's bitrate, like "320 kbps".

## Fixed
- **USB connection**: after unplugging at the wrong moment, a computer sometimes never found the player again until it was restarted. The player now reconnects every time.

## Known issues
- A charge-only USB cable only charges. If your computer doesn't see the player, try a cable that transfers data with a phone.
- Skins with their own fonts (Luna XP, Winamp and others) show boxes instead of Chinese, Japanese and Korean titles.
- After a sleep, Bluetooth headphones reconnect within a few seconds of waking. Headphones that went back to a phone meanwhile must be picked again in Settings → Bluetooth.
- WPA3-only Wi-Fi networks can't be joined; a "WPA2/WPA3 mixed" setting on the router works.
- Some players turned off by themselves during playback; the cause isn't found yet.
- Something wrong? Send an error report (Settings → System → Error Reports). **Restore Previous System** (Settings → System → About, tap Version seven times, then Diagnostics) takes you back to the version you had, with your data kept.

More details in plain words: **[Beta 9.3.18 report](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/validation/Y2-LINUX-1.0-BETA-9.3.18.md)**.

<!-- github-only -->

## Already running Y2Linux
Settings → System → Software Update → **Update Now**. Your music, playlists, settings, Wi-Fi networks and Bluetooth pairings stay. (On Beta 9.2.8 and older: Settings → About & Updates → Check for Updates → **Update Now**.)

## Install with the Innioasis Updater (easiest)
The community **Innioasis Updater CE** installs Y2Linux for you, on **Windows, macOS and Linux**. No SP Flash Tool needed.

1. Download Innioasis Updater CE for your computer from [innioasis.app](https://innioasis.app/guide.html#download-updater) and open it.
2. Choose **Y2**, then **Reborn (Y2Linux)** and the latest release.
3. Click **Install / Restore**, switch the Y2 off and connect it when the updater asks. Wait until it confirms, then unplug.
4. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** `system.img` from the Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0 into the **Firmware** folder on **Internal Storage**. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

Step-by-step guides for each computer: [Reborn (Y2Linux) install guide](https://innioasis.app/guides/reborn-y2linux-y2.html). The way back to stock is in the updater too: choose **Y2** and **Original Software**.

## Install with SP Flash Tool
You need SP Flash Tool v5.2032, a USB cable, **`Y2Linux-1.0.0-beta.9.3.18-first-install.zip`** below and the **Innioasis Y2 firmware package v3.2.0** from Innioasis (only this version works; it is also your way back to stock).

1. Unpack both.
2. SP Flash Tool → **Download Only** → load `MT6582_Android_scatter.txt` **from the Y2Linux zip**. Exactly BOOTIMG, RECOVERY, ANDROID and USRDATA are ticked.
3. Click Download and connect the switched-off Y2; wait for the green tick.
4. Unplug and press Power: the player sets up its Internal Storage (a few seconds), then Y2Linux and Reborn start, music works.
5. Connect the Y2 to the computer and **copy** (don't move) `system.img` from the Innioasis package into the **Firmware** folder on **Internal Storage**. The player takes the Wi-Fi/Bluetooth firmware from it and turns the radios on.

Full guide: [INSTALL](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md) · How updates work: [Recovery and updates](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/RECOVERY-AND-UPDATES.md) · Storage: [Storage](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/STORAGE.md) · [Audiobooks](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/AUDIOBOOKS.md) · Headphone settings: [Headphone output](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/HEADPHONE-OUTPUT.md) · [Error reports](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Linux/blob/main/docs/ERROR-REPORTS.md) · Skins: [skin guide](https://github.com/SchulzCode/Y2Reborn/blob/main/docs/skins.md)

## How it was tested
The USB fault was reproduced on the developer's player and is gone with this build (it reconnects half a second after plugging in; before, never). Every change has new tests, and the platform's full check, Reborn's workspace tests and the tests of the release images passed. Installed by update on the developer's player.
